name: Kingdom of Portugal
alt: Kingdom of Portugal and the Algarves
United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves (1815-1822)

predecessors.name: County of Portugal
predecessors.text: the County of Portugal, from the Minho to Coimbra (Cliopatria 1139-1146, 46,123 km2)

successors.name: Portuguese Republic (First Portuguese Republic)
successors.text: the metropole and the colonies, as the Republic's first Cliopatria shape (1911-1925, 2.2 M km2)

ledger.x: 1143: the Treaty of Zamora makes Portugal a kingdom.
1147: Lisbon falls to Afonso Henriques.
15 May 1147: Afonso Henriques takes Santarém.
1169: the shape holds the northern Alentejo.
1177: the southern part of the Alentejo conquest is gone (Cliopatria -9 cells, 38.4-38.64 N).

1188: the rest of the Alentejo conquest is gone (Cliopatria -23 cells, 38.68-39.57 N), the line of 1152 again; in 1184 'the Almohad caliph besieged Santarém, which was defended by Afonso's son Sancho'.
1189: Sancho I takes Silves.
1191: Silves is lost again.
1217: Alcácer do Sal is taken from the Almohads.
1227: Cliopatria adds 19 cells (38.79-39.57 N, 7.87-7.06 W: Portalegre and the Elvas country).
1241: Cliopatria adds the Baixo Alentejo and the eastern Algarve coast (+60 cells, 37.42-38.83 N).
ledger.cp: Muslim rulers of the Algarve and Alentejo (not named on the page)

ledger.x: 1249: the conquest of the Algarve is complete.
ledger.cp: Muslim rulers of the Algarve and Alentejo (not named on the page)

ledger.x: 1255: the seat moves from Coimbra to Lisbon.
1297: the Treaty of Alcañices fixes the frontier with Castile and gives Portugal Olivenza.
1385: the House of Aviz succeeds the Burgundian dynasty.
1419: the Portuguese reach Madeira.
1427: the Portuguese reach the Azores.
1580: António holds the Azores.
June 1580: the crown is contested.
25 August 1580: the mainland is lost to the claimant.
April 1581: Philip II of Spain becomes Philip I of Portugal and the crowns are joined.
1583: the last Portuguese resistance ends.
1 December 1640: Portugal recovers its independence.
1640: the House of Braganza takes the throne.
May 1644: the first dated battle of the long frontier war.
13 February 1668: the Treaty of Lisbon ends the war.
May 1706: an Allied force from Portugal enters Madrid and Zaragoza.
1708: Cliopatria drops the corridor in 1709.
20 May 1801: Spain attacks Portugal.
9 June 1801: the War of the Oranges ends (infobox '20 May - 9 June 1801').
6 June 1801: the Treaty of Badajoz cedes Olivenza.
1808: the court is in Rio de Janeiro.
August 1810: the French invade central Portugal.
April 1811: the French leave Portugal.
1815: the kingdom becomes the United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves, 'which existed between 1815 and 1822'.
1821: the court returns to Lisbon, the end of the 'seat of the Portuguese court' in Rio ('From 1808 to 1821').
7 September 1822: Brazil leaves.
5 October 1910: the monarchy falls.

wars.name: Portuguese Reconquista (Santarém and Lisbon to the Algarve)
wars.outcome: Portugal takes Santarém and Lisbon (1147), holds the northern Alentejo 1169-1176, Silves 1189-1191, and completes the Algarve in 1249.

wars.name: Almohad offensive against Silves
wars.outcome: Sancho I is 'King of Silves from 1189 until he lost the territory to Almohad control in 1191'.

wars.name: Castilian-Portuguese wars over the Algarve
wars.outcome: The dispute 'led to a series of wars between the two kingdoms'; the Treaty of Badajoz (1267) fixed 'the southern border between Castile and Portugal' on the Guadiana.

wars.name: Castilian-Portuguese war of 1295-1297
wars.outcome: Ended by the Treaty of Alcañices (1297): Portugal 'gained Olivença', the Algarve was reaffirmed and the treaty 'defined the modern borders'.

wars.name: War of the Portuguese Succession (1580 crisis)
wars.outcome: António is beaten at Alcântara on 25 August 1580; Philip II is recognised at Tomar in 1581; Terceira holds out 'until 1583'.

wars.name: Portuguese Restoration War
wars.outcome: Portugal wins: Spain recognised the House of Braganza by the Treaty of Lisbon (13 February 1668); Portugal kept its other colonies but not Ceuta.

wars.name: War of the Spanish Succession (Portuguese front)
wars.outcome: Portugal 'joined the Grand Alliance in May 1703'; an Allied force from Portugal entered Madrid and Zaragoza in 1706; the Allies were forced to retreat in 1710.

wars.name: War of the Oranges
wars.outcome: Spain wins in 21 days (20 May - 9 June 1801); the Treaty of Badajoz (6 June) cedes Olivenza.

wars.name: French invasions of Portugal
wars.outcome: Anglo-Portuguese victory: 'Marshal Masséna ordered a retreat at the beginning of March 1811' and returned to Spain in April 1811 (Lines of Torres Vedras page).

certainty.note: The Reconquista frontier (the Tagus line, the Alentejo and Algarve) is approximate; the Guadiana line of 1267 and the 1249 Algarve are the only fixed points.

The Treaty of Alcañices (1297) 'defined the modern borders between the two Iberian countries'; Olivenza is the exception after 1801; the 1706 Madrid corridor and the 1810-1811 French hold are occupations, not borders; the Atlantic islands…
